newsitem.title: USA: Vectra is seeking buyer for company.
newsitem.headline: Vectra is seeking buyer for company.

text.p: Vectra Technologies Inc said Wednesday it intends to sell the company.

The supplier of technologies and services to the nuclear power industry said the two key factors leading to this decision are a protracted schedule for restarting fabrication activities and unresolved contract renegotiations.
The company said a customer gave it written notification that it considers Vectra in default of its contract, which was delayed due to the company's hold on fabrication since late January.

Vectra said it believes contract defaults, to the extent that any exist, are properly covered under the force majeure conditions of its contract. It added it is trying to resolve the issue with the customer.
The company put its fabrication on hold after it received a request for information from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission January 17.
Vectra said in April it hoped to resume fabrication in May, following corrective actions implemented in response to the regulator's letter.
But company said Wednesday it has not yet resumed fabrication and concluded renegotiating its long-term contracts.
As a result, Vectra said it will take a $2.3 million charge in the second quarter to account for the estimated loss on its long-term contracts.
Vectra posted a $737,000 loss on revenues of 1.5 million in the first quarter, compared with a $40,000 profit on revenues of $24.5 million the year before.
Company spokesmen were not immediately available to elaborate.
